title: OpenAI Just Hired Uber India's Boss to Run Its Second-Biggest Market. It's Not Messing Around.
excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, an IIT-IIM alumnus who spent a decade building Uber across South Asia, will become OpenAI's most senior leader in India as the company races to convert ChatGPT's consumer popularity into institutional muscle.
body:
OpenAI has named Prabhjeet Singh, the outgoing president of Uber India and South Asia, as its first Managing Director for India — a hire that signals how seriously the ChatGPT maker now treats the subcontinent as a growth engine.

Singh, an alumnus of IIT Kharagpur and IIM Ahmedabad, will join OpenAI in September and become the company's most senior leader in the country. He will report to Kiran Mani, the recently appointed Managing Director for Asia Pacific, and will oversee everything from consumer and enterprise growth to partnerships, regulatory engagement, and day-to-day operations.

https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2070196105745518913

## India: OpenAI's Second-Largest Market

The appointment is not a symbolic one. India is now OpenAI's second-largest market after the United States, a fact driven by explosive consumer adoption of ChatGPT and a developer ecosystem that has embraced the company's APIs with unusual speed. CEO Sam Altman has publicly called India's AI uptake "amazing to watch," and the company opened its first India office in New Delhi in November 2025.



> **""We thank Prabhjeet for his leadership and lasting contributions in his decade-long journey with Uber," a spokesperson for the ride-hailing company said."**


But consumer traction alone does not build a business. OpenAI needs enterprise contracts, government partnerships, and regulatory goodwill — the exact toolkit that Singh honed over a decade at Uber. He joined the ride-hailing giant in 2015 as a general manager and head of strategy, and was elevated to president of India and South Asia in 2020. Under his leadership, Uber expanded its mobility footprint across India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh, navigating regulatory labyrinths that would test any executive's patience.

"We thank Prabhjeet for his leadership and lasting contributions in his decade-long journey with Uber," a spokesperson for the ride-hailing company said. "We remain deeply committed to our next phase of growth in India."


![Managing Director — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4e/Group_of_Fortune_500_CEOs_in_2015_%28cropped_to_remove_non-CEO%29.jpg)


## A Talent Pipeline From India's Boardrooms

Singh's appointment fits a broader pattern. Over the past year, OpenAI has assembled a serious India leadership team: Pragya Mishra, a Meta veteran, leads public policy and strategy; Kiran Mani, formerly of JioStar, runs the broader APAC operation. The hires collectively suggest that OpenAI is not building a sales office — it is building a regional headquarters.

The timing is deliberate. India's government has signalled that it wants to be a player in sovereign AI, not merely a consumer of American models. The India AI Mission, backed by ₹10,000 crore in public funding, is building compute infrastructure and nurturing homegrown models. A UAE-backed, Cerebras-powered supercomputer with 8 exaflops of capacity is being deployed in partnership with India's Centre for Development of Advanced Computing. And domestic players like Sarvam AI and Krutrim are building large language models optimised for Indian languages and regulatory conditions.

For OpenAI, the risk is that India's AI market matures around local alternatives before it can establish deep roots. Singh's mandate — bridging consumer popularity with institutional adoption — is the company's answer to that risk.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the roughly 4.5 million Indian-origin professionals working in technology worldwide, the appointment underlines a shift that has been gathering pace: the action in AI is no longer confined to San Francisco. India's engineering talent, its massive data footprint, and its government's willingness to court global AI firms have made the country a fulcrum of the industry's next chapter.

Singh himself embodies the trajectory. Trained at India's most selective institutions, shaped by a multinational's most complex market, and now recruited to lead the AI company that has captured the world's imagination — his career arc is one that a generation of IIT and IIM graduates will watch closely.

OpenAI did not disclose the financial terms of Singh's appointment or the headcount targets for its India office. But the message is clear enough: the company that changed how the world interacts with machines now considers India essential to what comes next.
